articles.title: Gol corta voos após preço do combustível dobrar; veja o que muda para passageiros | G1
articles.standfirst: Companhia afirma que o querosene de aviação representa cerca de 40% dos custos operacionais e orienta passageiros sobre como remarcar viagens, pedir crédito ou reembolso.
articles.summary: Companhia afirma que o querosene de aviação representa cerca de 40% dos custos operacionais e orienta passageiros sobre como remarcar viagens, pedir crédito ou reembolso.
articles.body:
A Gol está ajustando sua malha aérea, com redução ou suspensão de voos em algumas rotas, em meio à alta do combustível de aviação.

Até o momento, a empresa ainda não confirmou quais destinos foram cortados, mas enfatizou que as suspensões entram em vigor apenas em fevereiro de 2027.

Segundo a companhia, o preço do querosene de aviação (QAV) dobrou e o insumo representa cerca de 40% de seus custos operacionais.

Em nota, a empresa afirmou que o planejamento das rotas é um processo contínuo e acompanha as necessidades da operação . Segundo a Gol, as mudanças são feitas “sem qualquer distinção ou priorização regional”.

Até o momento, a empresa ainda não confirmou quais foram as rotas suspensas e modificadas, mas enfatizou que entram em vigor apenas em fevereiro de 2027.

A companhia informou que continuará oferecendo alternativas de viagem aos passageiros, seja por meio de voos com conexão — quando é necessário trocar de avião durante o trajeto —, seja por parcerias com outras empresas aéreas.

A Gol afirma ter mais de 60 acordos de codeshare e interline , modalidades de parceria que permitem às companhias comercializar voos em conjunto ou integrar trechos de uma mesma viagem.

Os passageiros que compraram passagens diretamente com a Gol podem solicitar remarcação, crédito ou reembolso pela Central de Atendimento , nos telefones 0300-115-2121, no Brasil, e +55 11 3471 2973, no exterior.

Quem adquiriu bilhetes com milhas deve gerenciar a reserva diretamente com a Smiles . Os contatos são 0300 115 7001, para clientes Smiles ou da categoria Prata; 0300 115 7007, para clientes Ouro e Diamante; e +55 11 991 824 233, pelo WhatsApp, para clientes Magno, com atendimento 24 horas.

Já os passageiros que compraram passagens por meio de agências de viagens devem procurar a própria agência para resolver questões relacionadas à reserva.

articles.title: Netflix corta cerca de 1.000 empregos  | G1
articles.standfirst: Redução atinge 6% do quadro de funcionários e afeta áreas de tecnologia, produto, jurídico e recursos humanos, informa o Wall Street Journal.
articles.summary: Redução atinge 6% do quadro de funcionários e afeta áreas de tecnologia, produto, jurídico e recursos humanos, informa o Wall Street Journal.
articles.body:
Evento da Netflix — Foto: REUTERS/Francis Mascarenhas

A Netflix vai demitir cerca de 6% de sua força de trabalho, o que representa aproximadamente 1.000 vagas. Esta é a maior rodada de cortes da empresa de streaming desde 2022, informou o jornal Wall Street Journal nesta quarta-feira (14).

Segundo o WSJ, a decisão foi comunicada aos funcionários por meio de um e-mail enviado na manhã de quarta-feira pelos co-presidentes executivos da companhia, Greg Peters e Ted Sarandos.

A maior parte das demissões ocorrerá nas equipes de produto, tecnologia, recursos humanos e no departamento jurídico.

No final do ano passado, a empresa contava com cerca de 16 mil funcionários em tempo integral. A companhia não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário feito pela agência de notícias Reuters.

Os cortes ocorrem em um momento de intensa concorrência pela atenção dos usuários em um mercado de mídia cada vez mais consolidado.

Para diversificar suas fontes de receita, a Netflix tem expandido sua atuação além do modelo de assinaturas, realizando investimentos em publicidade, programação ao vivo e jogos.

O cenário de consolidação do setor inclui movimentos recentes de concorrentes diretos. No início deste ano, a Netflix perdeu a disputa pelos ativos de estúdio e streaming da Warner Bros Discovery para a Paramount Skydance.

A Paramount concluiu a aquisição da Warner Bros neste mês por 110 bilhões de dólares , formando a Skydance, uma gigante de mídia que reúne um portfólio de estúdios de cinema e notícias.

A operação reúne marcas como Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures, HBO Max, Paramount+, CNN e CBS e coloca sob o comando de David Ellison um grupo que terá cerca de US$ 80 bilhões em dívidas.

A nova companhia passa a se chamar Skydance e terá suas ações negociadas na Bolsa de Nova York sob o código "SKYD". A mudança ocorreu nesta terça-feira, quando os papéis da empresa combinada deixaram de ser negociados na Nasdaq.

O acordo encerra uma das maiores disputas recentes pelo controle de ativos de Hollywood. A Paramount Skydance venceu uma concorrência que também envolveu a Netflix e atraiu o interesse de outras empresas, como a Comcast.

A fusão junta os estúdios responsáveis por franquias como Harry Potter, Batman, Missão: Impossível e Top Gun, além de serviços de streaming e grandes redes de televisão. A empresa passa a atuar em cinema, televisão, streaming e jornalismo.

articles.title: Minerais críticos e estratégicos concentram 57% dos empregos da mineração em 2025, diz ANM | G1
articles.standfirst: Do total de 226,6 mil empregos ocupados na indústria extrativa, segmento desses minerais representou 129,4 mil postos de trabalho.
articles.summary: Do total de 226,6 mil empregos ocupados na indústria extrativa, segmento desses minerais representou 129,4 mil postos de trabalho.
articles.body:
As atividades ligadas aos minerais críticos e estratégicos concentraram 57% dos empregos da indústria extrativa mineral brasileira em 2025, segundo dados disponibilizados pela Agência Nacional de Mineração (ANM).

➡️ Do total de 226,6 mil empregos no setor, o segmento desses minerais representou 129,4 mil postos de trabalho.

Dos 129,4 mil empregos ligados a esses minerais, 51.714 são ocupados por trabalhadores com mão de obra qualificada. Esse contingente equivale a 23% de todos os empregos da indústria extrativa mineral brasileira.

Já os trabalhadores com ensino superior somam 30.707, o equivalente a 14% do total de postos da indústria extrativa mineral do país.

E os homens predominam nessas atividades: eles respondem por 78% dos empregos relacionados aos minerais críticos e estratégicos, enquanto as mulheres ocupam 22% dos postos.

Os números fazem parte do Portal de Minerais Críticos e Estratégicos, lançado nesta tarde pela Agência Nacional de Mineração (ANM).

Entre os municípios com maior número de trabalhadores em atividades relacionadas aos MCE estão Parauapebas (PA), com 8.234 empregos; Nova Lima (MG), com 8.218; e Congonhas (MG), com 7.114.

Em 2025, o salário mediano dos trabalhadores com níveis fundamental, médio e superior foi, respectivamente, de R$ 3.218,08, R$ 4.142,24 e R$ 11.856,16.

Minerais críticos: projeto aprovado na Câmara quer garantir que o Brasil não seja apenas exportador de matéria-prima — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Após uma longa discussão, o governo sancionou, no mês passado, a Política Nacional de Minerais Críticos e Estratégicos, que estabelece diretrizes para as etapas de pesquisa, lavra, beneficiamento, transformação mineral e mineração urbana.

A política considera como críticos os minerais cujo abastecimento está sujeito a riscos capazes de afetar setores essenciais da economia.

Já os estratégicos são aqueles considerados importantes para o desenvolvimento tecnológico e regional, para a balança comercial ou para a redução das emissões de gases de efeito estufa.

🔍 O Brasil ainda não tem uma lista oficial de minerais classificados como críticos e estratégicos. A tarefa ficará a cargo do Conselho Nacional para Industrialização de Minerais Críticos e Estratégicos (CIMCE), também criado pela política.

Esses minerais têm aplicações em áreas diversas, como transição energética, digitalização, defesa e indústria de alta tecnologia.

Lítio, níquel, cobalto, grafita e manganês são usados em baterias de íon-lítio, por exemplo. Os veículos elétricos, por sua vez, também utilizam minerais como lítio, cobre e níquel, além de terras raras, em sua composição.

A política também prevê instrumentos como:

Programa Federal de Beneficiamento e Transformação de Minerais Críticos e Estratégicos;

Rede de pesquisa, desenvolvimento tecnológico e formação profissional.

articles.title: Dollar advances to highest since May 2025 on Fed hike views
articles.summary: The dollar strengthened to the highest level in over a year as hot US inflation reading pushed traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise int...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The dollar strengthened to the highest level in over a year as hot US inflation reading pushed traders to add to bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index surged Wednesday past its November high. The gauge rose as much as 0.4% to the highest level since May 2025. US consumer prices advanced at the fastest pace in five months on rising fuel costs, according to Bureau of Labor Statistics data.

"Hotter than expected CPI has given a boost to the Dollar this morning as traders price in further tightening from the Fed," said Andrew Hazlett, a foreign-exchange trader at Monex Inc.

The dollar has surged nearly 3% for the four-week period ending Oct. 9 to post its longest winning streak since early 2025. The rally has been fueled by traders' rate predictions since the Fed raised rates for the first time in three years last month. That move has been followed by hawkish remarks from central bank officials. The market is now pricing in more than 90 basis points of rate increases in the US.

Elevated oil prices due to the ongoing war in Iran and heightened concern over fiscal and political risks in France have boosted demand for the haven currency. The war has also been lifting global yields. While central bank policymakers in other major countries are also gearing to raise borrowing costs to stem price growth, not all economies can handle the same amount of rate hikes as the US through September.

A widening interest-rate gap is favoring the dollar, with many strategists on Wall Street rethinking their outlook for the US currency. Speculative traders boosted their bullish stance on the dollar in the week through Oct. 6, holding more than $35 billion in wagers tied to the dollar rising, Commodity Futures Trading Commission data show.

articles.title: US inflation accelerates to 3.7% in September as gasoline prices surge
articles.summary: US consumer inflation accelerated in September as a surge in gasoline prices and firmer underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden for
articles.body: US consumer inflation accelerated in September as a surge in gasoline prices and firmer underlying price pressures added to the cost-of-living burden for American households ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The consumer price index (CPI) rose 3.7 per cent year-on-year in September, up from 3.4 per cent in August, the US Labor Department said on Wednesday. On a monthly basis, consumer prices increased 0.6 per cent, compared with a 0.4 per cent rise in the previous month.The annual inflation rate was slightly above economists' expectations of 3.6 per cent, according to a Reuters poll, while the monthly increase was in line with forecasts.The latest figures reflect the impact of higher energy costs following the US-Israeli war with Iran, which began in late February and disrupted oil and gas supplies. Rising costs have added to concerns over affordability, a key issue ahead of the midterm elections, in which President Donald Trump's Republican Party is seeking to retain control of Congress.Gasoline prices drive inflationGasoline prices were a major contributor to the monthly increase in consumer prices, rising sharply in September. US Energy Information Administration data showed gasoline prices climbed 7.1 per cent during the month, while the Labor Department's CPI report recorded a 9.1 per cent increase.Higher fuel costs have also pushed up expenses across other sectors, including transportation and travel. Airfares rose 1.2 per cent in September and were up around 22 per cent from a year earlier, while hotel prices increased 2 per cent over the month.Rising fuel and transportation expenses have also increased costs for businesses, raising the risk that companies will pass some of the additional burden on to consumers through higher prices for goods and services.Grocery prices offered some relief, declining 0.1 per cent in September, although they remained 1.8 per cent higher than a year earlier.Core inflation also picks upUnderlying price pressures remained firm even after excluding volatile food and energy components. Core CPI rose 2.6 per cent in September from a year earlier, compared with 2.4 per cent in August.On a monthly basis, core inflation increased 0.3 per cent, matching the previous month's rise. Price increases across a range of goods and services suggest that inflationary pressures extend beyond the energy sector.Economists have also pointed to strong investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centres as a factor pushing up the cost of semiconductors, computer equipment and electronic devices.“The report was worse than expected,” Bill Adams, chief US economist at Fifth Third Bank, said in a note to clients, adding that price increases were widespread across durable goods, nondurable goods and services.What it means for Federal ReserveThe inflation data could complicate the Federal Reserve's decisions on interest rates as policymakers weigh persistent price pressures against the impact of tighter monetary policy on economic growth.The Fed raised its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points last month to a range of 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent, marking its first rate increase in three years. It has indicated that further increases could follow if inflation remains elevated.Financial markets had assigned a roughly 22 per cent probability of another rate increase at the Fed's October 27-28 meeting before the September CPI report, according to CME Group's FedWatch Tool.However, some economists expect policymakers to hold rates steady at the upcoming meeting and assess further economic data before deciding on another increase. Higher borrowing costs can help moderate demand and slow price increases, but they cannot directly address supply disruptions caused by geopolitical conflicts.The latest inflation figures come as the cost of living remains a major concern for American voters ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.The September inflation report is also important for millions of Americans receiving Social Security benefits. The annual cost-of-living adjustment for 2027 is based on inflation data for urban wage earners and clerical workers during the third quarter of 2026 compared with the corresponding period a year earlier.The Senior Citizens League has projected a 3.5 per cent increase in Social Security benefits for 2027, up from the 2.8 per cent adjustment for 2026. articles.summary: United Airlines is upgrading its fleet to high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi. Now, it's making the case for members of competitor loyalty programs to switch to Mileag...
articles.body:

United Airlines is rolling out high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi on flights and inviting travelers to try the service with a valuable new MileagePlus status match.

United ( UAL ) has spent much of this year upgrading its flights to have Starlink access. A recent analyst note from Sheila Kahyaoglu at Jefferies said Starlink is already available on just under 600 United aircraft. That includes about 300 regional jets and 300 mainline aircraft.

That's an increase from the over 450 aircraft United reported in its July earnings. Earlier this year, Ankit Gupta, United's chief air operations officer, said close to 1,000 aircraft would have Starlink by the end of 2026.

United says it expects 50% of its mainline fleet to have Starlink by the end of this year, and 100% to be equipped with high-speed Wi-Fi by the end of 2027.

The quick rollout puts United ahead of other major U.S. airlines in switching to high-speed internet in-flight. American Airlines ( AAL ) is also upgrading to Starlink, though it will begin installing the service in 2027. Delta Air Lines ( DAL ) offers free Wi-Fi to SkyMiles members on flights and is making "meaningful enhancements" to that service this year, but will begin upgrading to Amazon Leo (another high-speed service) in 2028.

In the meantime, United is using its advanced Wi-Fi service to entice travelers to switch from American and Delta to its MileagePlus loyalty program via a status match offer. Until Oct. 15, elite-status members of either competing airline can get a status match with United lasting through Jan. 31, 2028.

Here's what to know about United's Starlink availability and MileagePlus perks for those who take advantage of the match.

On flights with Starlink Wi-Fi enabled, United MileagePlus members can connect for free. Without a MileagePlus account, travelers won't be able to access the Starlink connection.

United's first wide-body Starlink flight across the Atlantic was on June 22, from Newark to London. The airline said passengers could expect the service on routes between its major hubs in the U.S., including Newark, Washington D.C., Houston, and San Francisco, and popular international destinations — London, Paris, Tokyo, and more.

While travelers won't know the Starlink status of their flights at booking, they can find out whether they're on an upgraded plan when checking in for a flight.

For flights that don't yet have Starlink, United still offers Wi-Fi options. Access costs $8 or 800 miles for United MileagePlus members and $10 for everyone else. That's for domestic and short-haul international flights; prices for other international flights can vary.

As it rolls out Starlink access — and amid an ongoing dispute between SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Delta CEO Ed Bastian — United is making its faster Wi-Fi a selling point for frequent travelers who may be looking for a change.

Through Oct. 15, travelers with elite status on Delta or American Airlines can get their status matched within the United MileagePlus program. The status match will last through Jan. 31, 2028.

Members can submit their request on United's website by completing a form and uploading proof of status within either the Delta SkyMiles or American AAdvantage loyalty program. That request will get approved within three days and remain active for 90 days.

Within the 90-day period, members must also meet a certain spending threshold on United or United Express flights to maintain the status match until January 2028. The required spend depends on the status being matched:

articles.title: Canada's Fairfax to buy 60.2% stake in IDBI Bank for Rs 53,000 crore; largest FDI in an Indian bank
articles.summary: Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings is set to acquire a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank for approximately Rs 53,000 crore ($5.5 billion).
articles.body: Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holdings is set to acquire a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank for approximately Rs 53,000 crore ($5.5 billion). The transaction would rank as the largest foreign investment in an Indian bank. It marks a big step forward in India's long-pending efforts to privatise state-owned banking assets.The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs has approved M/s 10955230 Canada Inc, a subsidiary of Fairfax, as the strategic buyer for the combined stakes held by the government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC). The government will sell its 30.48 per cent holding for around Rs 26,620 crore, while LIC will divest its 30.24 per cent stake for approximately Rs 26,440 crore.The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs' approval brings to a close a process that has stretched over nine years. Valuation disagreements had repeatedly complicated the sale. In February 2026, initial bids from Fairfax and Emirates NBD came in below the government's undisclosed reserve price, forcing a pause in the process. The bidding exercise was subsequently revived, and the revised offers were placed before the cabinet committee for consideration.Fairfax, led by Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, will pay Rs 81 per share. This is above the benchmark fair value of Rs 75.99 arrived at by two independent valuation agencies, according to an official statement.Biggest foreign investment in an Indian bankThe proposed sale is the biggest transaction in the banking sector and a major development in the prolonged effort to privatise IDBI Bank and reduce government ownership of commercial enterprises.The transaction is expected to be completed before the end of FY27. Once the deal goes through, the government will withdraw its representatives from IDBI Bank's board.Emirates NBD's acquisition of a 60 per cent stake in RBL Bank was valued at $3 billion. The Fairfax-IDBI Bank transaction would also exceed MUFG Bank's purchase of a 20 per cent stake in Shriram Finance for Rs 39,618 crore. That deal was described as the largest cross-border investment in India's financial-services sector, but the IDBI Bank transaction is larger by around Rs 13,000 crore.The proposed acquisition is also significantly bigger than Sumitomo Mitsui's $2 billion deal for Fullerton India Credit and PayU's $4.7 billion acquisition of BillDesk, which was the largest financial-services transaction of its period.The disinvestment process was initiated in 2022 but suffered a setback earlier this year when the initial bids received were lower than the government's reserve price.Following the announcement on Wednesday, IDBI Bank shares rose 9.07% to close at Rs 90.44 apiece on the BSE.Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman described the deal as a "milestone", saying "having supported the bank's recovery, we are now enabling its next phase of growth through the infusion of Foreign Direct Investment while retaining a minority stake"."This will not only strengthen the banking ecosystem but also help banking services surpass global benchmarks. It reinforces that India's growth story is strong, its economy is resilient, and the government's commitment to reform is unwavering," she added.Regulatory approvals neededThe transaction cannot be completed until it receives the necessary regulatory clearances. These include approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), which will carry out a "fit and proper" assessment, as well as clearances from the Competition Commission of India (CCI) and other statutory authorities.Before the sale can be finalised, Fairfax will have to establish its credentials with the RBI and submit a roadmap outlining how it intends to meet the regulator's requirements.The company will also be required to make an open offer to public shareholders, unless the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) grants a waiver.Under RBI regulations, promoters are permitted to hold a maximum stake of 26 per cent in a bank.Fairfax will have up to 15 years to meet this requirement, Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) Secretary Arunish Chawla said. The promoter will also be subject to a five-year lock-in period, he added.Fairfax already owns a 40 per cent stake in Kerala-based CSB Bank. Following the IDBI Bank acquisition, it will have to either merge the two lenders or exit its investment in CSB Bank, which is based in South India.Chawla said the incoming promoter would be required to preserve IDBI Bank's existing name, brand and customer relationships for a minimum of three years.Addressing concerns among employees, he said they had no reason to worry. The transfer of management, he added, had been discussed with all stakeholders.LIC, meanwhile, will be required to reduce its holding in IDBI Bank from 19 per cent to 15 per cent within two years.The IDBI Bank deal could mark a turning point for India's banking industry by establishing a potential model for privatising other state-owned lenders, where government ownership continues to be predominant.It will also offer a test of whether investors are willing to take control of a large Indian bank while navigating stringent regulatory conditions and the challenges involved in running a financial institution.The government, however, has described the proposed divestment as a "strategic restructuring". It has maintained that the Centre and LIC will together retain a 34 per cent stake in the bank.The sale would come after the Tata Group's takeover of Air India, completed in January 2022. Tata had won the bid for the national carrier in October 2021 with an offer of Rs 18,000 crore, comprising Rs 2,700 crore in cash and the assumption of Rs 15,300 crore in debt.You use AI every day. articles.title: Precio de la luz por horas mañana, jueves 15 de octubre: cuándo es más barata y más cara
articles.standfirst: El precio de la luz se encarece en jueves
articles.summary: El precio de la luz se encarece en jueves
articles.body: El precio medio de la electricidad hoy se sitúa en 193,11 €/MWh, lo que supone un incremento de 6,66 € respecto al día anterior, que cerró en 186,45 €/MWh. Este aumento se produce en un jueves, en el que se prevén horas con precios significativamente diferentes. A lo largo del día, es crucial identificar las horas más caras y más baratas para optimizar el consumo. La luz es más cara durante las horas pico de la tarde y la noche, especialmente entre las 20:00 y las 22:00. Durante este intervalo, los precios alcanzan su máxima expresión, con un costo de 287.73 €/MWh a las 20:00 y 248.47 €/MWh a las 21:00. Además, se observa un bloque continuo de precios elevados desde las 18:00 hasta las 22:00, donde los valores superan constantemente los 230 €/MWh, siendo notablemente costosas las horas de 19:00 a 21:00. Esto revela un claro patrón en la demanda de energía durante estas franjas horarias. Las mejores oportunidades de ahorro en el precio de la luz se concentran durante las primeras horas del día y en la franja del mediodía. En particular, los tramos más destacados son de 12:00 a 15:00 donde los precios son especialmente bajos, alcanzando el valor más bajo de 68.24 €/MWh a las 13:00. Además, se observa una ventana amplia de precios reducidos desde las 10:00 con 187.06 €/MWh hasta las 15:00 con 85.08 €/MWh, lo que proporciona varias horas para maximizar el ahorro. En contraste, las horas de mayor tarifa se ubican entre las 19:00 y 21:00, donde los precios superan los 270 €/MWh. En el análisis de las franjas horarias de hoy, destaca una notable diferencia de precios entre la hora más cara y la más barata, que alcanza los 219,49 €/MWh, lo que resalta la volatilidad del mercado eléctrico y la oportunidad que tienen los consumidores de gestionar su consumo para maximizar el ahorro.

articles.title: Bending Spoons stock soars on new Berkshire Hathaway investment
articles.summary: Bending Spoons stock soared as much as 54% in morning trading on Wednesday after the Italian tech company said Berkshire Hathaway will invest another $330 mi...
articles.body:
Bending Spoons stock ( BSP ) soared as much as 54% in morning trading on Wednesday after the Italian tech company said Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK-B ) will invest another $330 million in it.

The stock hit $58 per share at one point in the morning, just shy of its intraday record of $58.94 set on Aug. 11, before settling back to a gain of about 38% around 11 a.m. ET. If the gain holds, Wednesday would be the stock's best day since its July 1 market debut.

Trading volume passed 9.8 million, more than four times the stock's three-month daily average, according to Yahoo Finance data.

Berkshire is buying the new stock in a private placement at $33 per share, about 13% below Tuesday's close, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Wednesday.

The deal lifts Berkshire's stake to 4%, the company said. Berkshire invested $600 million in Bending Spoons at its initial public offering in July. The IPO was priced at $29.

The stock is up around 80% from its IPO price, giving Bending Spoons a market value of about $33 billion.

Bending Spoons said it will use the money for general corporate purposes and new acquisitions. It expects the deal to close in the fourth quarter. Neither the announcement nor the filing included a comment from Berkshire.

"For decades now, Berkshire Hathaway has been among the finest and most respected capital allocators in the world, and is a longstanding inspiration for Bending Spoons," CEO and co-founder Luca Ferrari said in the announcement .

"Bending Spoons continuously evaluates M&A opportunities, and our pipeline remains strong," said co-founder Francesco Patarnello, who leads the company's acquisitions. He said the investment "will further enhance our financial flexibility and ability to pursue attractive acquisitions."

articles.title: Federal watchdog says 9 large US banks denied service to customers over political or religious views
articles.summary: A federal banking watchdog determined that nine banks' sweeping internal guidelines lacked objective, risk-based criteria, effectively shutting out legitimat...
articles.body:
The Comptroller of the Currency says the nation's nine largest banks denied financial services to customers based on their political, religious, or social beliefs, according to a regulatory review released Wednesday.

The OCC reviewed nearly 100,000 complaints and received approximately 50,000 documents from JPMorgan Chase Bank, Bank of America, Citibank, Wells Fargo Bank, U.S. Bank, Capital One, PNC Bank, TD Bank, and BMO Bank regarding their policies, procedures, practices, and individual customer decisions.

The federal banking watchdog determined that the banks' sweeping internal guidelines lacked objective, risk-based criteria, effectively shutting out legitimate customers and businesses based on ideological leanings rather than financial risk.

The OCC said its findings reveal a systematic effort within the banking sector to restrict access for politically sensitive industries through both public and nonpublic policies.

Federal regulators found that lenders restricted certain sectors' access to financial services, including oil and gas exploration; coal mining; firearms or ammunition manufacturing or distribution; construction or operation of detention facilities; and the manufacturing, distribution or online retail of tobacco or e-cigarettes.

The Trump administration has voiced growing concerns over "de-banking" and the use of the financial system to achieve social and political objectives.

"Today's report provides irrefutable evidence that the nation's largest banks have denied, debanked, and discriminated against customers and lawful businesses," said Comptroller of the Currency Jonathan Gould. "Americans should have access to financial services regardless of their beliefs, affiliations, or political views. "

All nine banks report having reassessed the role of reputation risk in decisions to accept or terminate new customers, according to the OCC's report. Several banks said they had minimized reliance on reputation risk, and bank employees now must consider it in the context of other financial or business consequences, including credit risk, money laundering and terrorist financing risk.

The Bank Policy Institute, a lobbying group that represents the banks, said in a statement in reaction to the report, "We support efforts to establish clear and consistent standards that promote access while maintaining sound risk management, including the administration's recent efforts to prioritize supervisory attention on material financial risk and rather than reputational risk."

articles.title: India remains top Russian crude buyer in September despite 29% fall in imports since July
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India remained the world's largest destination for Russian crude oil in September, although imports fell nearly 29 per cent from July levels as
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India remained the world's largest destination for Russian crude oil in September, although imports fell nearly 29 per cent from July levels as Chinese refiners stepped up purchases and tightened the availability of Russian supplies, according to ship-tracking data from Kpler.India imported around 1.82 million barrels per day (bpd) of Russian crude in September, compared with China's 1.49 million bpd. Indian imports had peaked at 2.6 million bpd in June and 2.57 million bpd in July before declining to 2.02 million bpd in August.The moderation comes amid US pressure on countries buying Russian oil, including through tariffs and sanctions. However, analysts say the decline in India's purchases also reflects supply constraints and growing competition from China, rather than being solely a response to Washington's actions."The recent moderation in India's Russian imports is not simply a response to US tariff pressure; tighter availability and stronger competition from China have also played an important role," said Sumit Ritolia, senior manager (modelling) at Kpler.Chinese refiners have increased their purchases of Russian crude in recent months, partly because of reduced access to Iranian oil, adding to competition for available supplies.Based on cargoes currently being tracked, Kpler expects India's Russian crude imports to remain broadly stable at around 1.8 million to 1.9 million bpd in October.US pressure over Russian oil, but a diesel deal with MoscowIndia's continued reliance on Russian crude comes amid Washington's efforts to discourage purchases of Russian energy. US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 into law in September. The legislation authorises tariffs of up to 100 per cent on imports from countries buying Russian oil, but gives the president discretion over whether and how to apply them. India and China are among the major buyers potentially affected.However, Washington's own approach to Russian energy has also shifted in response to rising fuel costs.On October 9, Trump announced an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin under which Russia would supply more than 300,000 tonnes of diesel to US and global markets, followed by additional shipments. The Trump administration also temporarily eased US sanctions on Russian fuel to facilitate the arrangement, which was aimed at increasing supplies and containing prices ahead of the November midterm elections.The move nevertheless drawn criticism from Ukraine and some European leaders, who argue that purchases of Russian energy could provide Moscow with additional revenue during its war against Ukraine.Meanwhile, alongside Russian supplies, Venezuelan crude has regained a place in India's import mix this year after remaining largely absent in recent years. Shipments began accelerating from April, according to Kpler.Venezuela exported around 250,000 bpd of crude to India in August and 257,000 bpd in September. The US remained the larger destination, receiving approximately 452,000 bpd in August and 563,000 bpd in September.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Apple retakes $5 trillion market cap, only second company to eclipse milestone number
articles.summary: Apple's market cap crossed the $5 trillion mark on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Apple's ( AAPL ) market capitalization once again crossed the $5 trillion mark on Wednesday, just months after it first touched the threshold in late July.

It's been just under a year since Apple's market cap topped $4 trillion in October 2025. The company's stock price is up roughly 26% year to date and nearly 40% over the past 12 months.

Apple stock climbed more than 1% Wednesday.

The milestone comes a little more than a month after John Ternus took over as Apple CEO from Tim Cook , who stepped down on Sept. 1, a day after Apple debuted its HomeView smart home hub amid a renewed effort to grab share in the smart home market.

Amazon ( AMZN ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ) currently dominate that space .

Apple has also benefited from strong iPhone sales throughout 2026 on the back of a renewed upgrade cycle.

The company has also finally fleshed out its AI strategy after investors heavily criticized the iPhone maker for initially falling behind in the AI race and struggling to catch up.

Apple unveiled its Apple Intelligence platform at its WWDC event in 2024, but the company delayed a number of features, leaving Wall Street to question Apple's ability to compete with rivals, including Google and Microsoft ( MSFT ).

But the company has since won a reprieve.

It has partnered with Google to use some of the search giant's AI models and rolled out a number of major updates to Apple Intelligence, including its Siri AI, though the software is still in beta.

And then there's the iPhone Duo foldable, which, at $1,999, could boost the iPhone line's average selling price and the company's bottom line. Apple is also preparing to launch its first touch-screen MacBook and revamped iPads later this month, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman .

But Apple is also working to contend with the ongoing memory and storage shortage, which has forced it to raise prices on its iPhones, iPads, and Macs, driving fears that sales could take a hit.

articles.title: Why the housing market is in for 'a challenging couple months'
articles.summary: Mortgage rates rose sharply in September, starting the month well below 7% and ending around 7.5%.
articles.body:
The housing market was weak even before mortgage rates jumped, setting up more strain to come, Realtor.com chief economist Danielle Hale said.

"The housing market was not in a robust place to start off with. And then with mortgage rates moving up the way they have, I think we're going to see a challenging couple months ahead," Hale told Yahoo Finance.

Mortgage rates rose sharply in September , starting the month well below 7% and ending around 7.5%.

September home sales data released this week showed sales rose 1.5% last month from August to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.99 million, according to the National Association of Realtors. Compared to a year ago, sales are down 2.2%.

That data largely reflects homes that went under contract in August, when rates were beginning to rise but were well below recent highs — meaning sales activity for October could be especially weak.

"The housing market that people are facing today is in a very different place than the housing market that drove these September home sales," Hale said.

She noted that mortgage rates in August were closer to 6.7%. The average rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate loan was 7.58% on Wednesday, according to Mortgage News Daily.

"The housing market has some more headwinds on the horizon given where mortgage rates are today," Hale said.

Molly Moorhead is economics editor for Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: AI infra startup Modal raises $750 mn at $15.7 bn valuation
articles.summary: Modal Labs raises $750m led by Accel at a $15.7bn valuation, topping $1bn annualized revenue run rate as demand surges for AI infrastructure and sandboxes.
articles.body: BENGALURU: AI infrastructure startup Modal Labs, co-founded by Delhi-raised computer scientist and Olympiad gold medallist Akshat Bubna, has raised $750 million that values the company at $15.7 billion. The fundraise comes as the five-year-old company crossed $1 billion in annualised revenue run rate, fuelled by growing demand for infrastructure that powers AI applications.The latest valuation is more than three times the $4.6 billion Modal was valued at in May this year, when it raised $355 million in a Series C round. The company’s valuation has risen more than 14-fold since September 2025, when it was worth $1.1 billion.Accel led the latest round, with Kleiner Perkins joining as an investor. Existing backers Menlo Ventures, General Catalyst, Redpoint, Lux Capital and Bain Capital Ventures also participated, the company said on Wednesday.Modal said usage of its platform had tripled in the five months since its previous funding round, while the business had grown more than 15-fold year-on-year. Its annualised run rate, which reflects the pace of revenue extrapolated over a year rather than revenue earned in the preceding 12 months, has climbed from about $300 million in May to over $1 billion.Founded in 2021 by Bubna and Swedish engineer Erik Bernhardsson, Modal provides computing infrastructure that allows companies to develop, run and scale AI applications without having to manage their own servers or computing hardware. Its platform now draws capacity from more than 20 cloud providers, allowing developers to access computing power as demand rises or falls.One of Modal’s fastest-growing businesses is Sandboxes, a product that allows AI agents to execute code in isolated environments. Launched in 2023, the product alone has reached a $300 million annualised run rate, the company said. Modal claims it has launched nearly three billion such environments to date and can support up to one million running simultaneously.The surge reflects growing adoption of AI coding agents, which need computing environments to execute programs, test results and carry out tasks. Modal said its infrastructure is used by companies including DoorDash, Cognition, Ramp and Runway, as well as robotics firms Physical Intelligence, Generalist AI and 1X.Modal is also expanding its products for AI model training and inference, the process of running trained models to generate outputs. Its latest launches include tools for training models across multiple machines and new capabilities for running AI applications.Bubna, who became the first Indian student to win gold at the International Olympiad in Informatics in 2014, previously told TOI that conventional cloud infrastructure was not designed for the demands of modern AI.In an interview last year, Bubna explained that Modal’s approach was to build its own software systems rather than depend on tools originally created for older computing applications. “One of the things programming competitions teach you is that most things are pretty solvable. You get used to solving harder problems,” he said at the time.The company has also expanded its workforce sharply. Modal had around 70 employees when Bubna spoke to TOI last year. articles.title: Groww Q2 profit up 54% to Rs 725 cr
articles.summary: Groww Q2 net profit jumps 54% to Rs 725 crore; revenue up 44% to Rs 1,541 crore as margin lending grows and US stock investing is tested.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Online investment platform Groww’s net profit rose 54% from a year earlier to Rs 725 crore for the September quarter. Its revenue rose 44% to Rs 1,541 crore, with margin lending and commodity derivatives contributing a larger share.Sequentially, however, net profit fell 1.4% from Rs 735 crore in the June quarter, while revenue dipped 0.5% from Rs 1,549 crore.The company is also testing a US stock investing product, co-founder and CEO Lalit Keshre told analysts. He described it as a very early test and said there was no fixed timeline for a launch. “The feedback is really good from the customers,” he said, adding that Groww would continue refining the product based on their responses.Equity derivatives revenue fell 14.3% from the previous quarter. Groww attributed most of the decline to market adjustments following Sebi’s introduction of a closing auction system in August, which changed how closing prices are determined for certain stocks. The segment remained its biggest income contributor, but its share fell to 44.8% from 56.9% a year earlier.Management said proposed changes to derivatives settlement could help normalise trading activity. It cautioned that volumes would also depend on factors such as market volatility.Meanwhile, Groww’s outstanding margin trading loan book grew to Rs 4,351 crore from Rs 1,668 crore a year earlier. The facility allows customers to borrow funds to buy shares.Chief financial officer Ishan Bansal said Groww had tightened its lending policies and was examining exposure to individual stocks across the industry, alongside its own positions.“We have to start looking at the industry level book as well,” he said. Groww is excluding some stocks from its approved lending list or requiring higher margins. In some cases, Bansal said, it finances only 20% of the value, limiting its exposure if prices fall sharply.Expenses rose 29% to Rs 556 crore. Technology costs increased because of more trading days, greater use of AI and higher computing costs. Groww also incurred Rs 13 crore in one-time client reimbursements following an operational issue at a third-party market infrastructure institution. Management said delayed files on an expiry day had caused the issue.Marketing spending fell sequentially because IPL-related expenses incurred in the June quarter did not recur. articles.title: News outlets win a round against Trump’s press ban — but the fight is far from over
articles.summary: News outlets and press freedom advocates are cheering the latest court ruling against President Donald Trump’s press ban, while cautioning that he will keep trying to punish news coverage he dislikes.
articles.body: News outlets and press freedom advocates are cheering the latest court ruling against President Donald Trump’s press ban, while cautioning that he will keep trying to punish news coverage he dislikes. CNN chairman and editor-in-chief Mark Thompson said news outlets have to be “forever vigilant” about First Amendment rights. The Justice Department plans to appeal the latest ruling, and its antitrust division is also probing the five major TV networks over how the White House TV pool operates. With all that in mind, Thompson said it’s necessary to “be prepared to fight and to go on fighting.” “I mean, this topic is one we’re never going to back down from,” he said. “And no matter how many court cases, investigations, court appearances and all the expense that that entails, we will fight this one to the end.” On Tuesday night, US District Judge Timothy P. Kelly ruled that Trump’s mid-September ban of CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House likely violated the First Amendment. Kelly issued a preliminary injunction protecting journalists’ access to the White House while the lawsuit continues. “It’s not the end of the matter, I mean, sooner or later there may be a trial,” Thompson said in an interview on CNN. “But I think it’s a really big boost — the judge essentially saying our complaint is likely to succeed” at trial. Thompson called it “a vote of confidence in free speech” and the public’s right “to hear their political leader held to account by the press.” Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press president Bruce D. Brown noted that the ruling “protects not only CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, but all the other holders of White House passes who continued to work under the threat of retaliation.” But other tests involving White House access are likely. In a recent interview with TIME, Trump complained about The New York Times and said “maybe they’ll be next” to be banned. And even with a temporary restraining order in place earlier this month, the White House blocked CNN from boarding Air Force One, apparently citing ongoing litigation with The Associated Press. “We welcome Judge Kelly’s order, but we are concerned that the White House continues to ban some news outlets from the White House press pool, where President Trump speaks the most with reporters,” Katie Fallow, the deputy litigation director at the Knight First Amendment Institute, said in a statement. “We are also concerned that the White House is still threatening to ban other journalists from the White House because he disagrees with their reporting,” Fallow added. “That practice is unconstitutional, and harms both the press and the public, which relies on journalists to report independently on the president and his administration.” Nora Benavidez, senior counsel at Free Press, said in a Wednesday statement Kelly’s ruling “affirms that presidential cherry-picking of newsroom access violates core First Amendment principles. A powerful district court ruling citing strong First Amendment precedent isn’t the end, however.” Trump has escalated his anti-media rhetoric in recent months, sometimes even claiming that responsible reporting is “treasonous.” The Justice Department, the FCC and other agencies have followed his lead and taken action against individual journalists and news outlets in ways that have been widely denounced by First Amendment groups. And Trump has trumpeted his administration’s pressure campaign against the press. On Tuesday night, during a rally in Alaska, he pointed to FCC chairman Brendan Carr and quipped that Carr is “the most feared man in government.” Carr has pursued or threatened multiple investigations into broadcasters, including a new probe of ABC News over a since-corrected report about business investments involving Trump’s sons. His agency is currently pursuing a highly unusual challenge of ABC’s local station licenses, a move Disney is challenging in court as unconstitutional retaliation. Numerous former FCC officials of both parties have decried the “weaponization” of the FCC under Carr.

articles.title: Currency depreciation key headwind for foreign investors: Blackstone's Gray
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Its $50 billion investments in India place Blackstone among the top 10 business houses.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Its $50 billion investments in India place Blackstone among the top 10 business houses. The world's largest alternative asset manager plans to double its investments in the next five years mainly in private equity and real estate, and expand into infrastructure, credit and growth investing. In an interview with TOI, Jonathan Gray, president and COO of Blackstone, speaks of how the focus is on building businesses.Despite being the fastest-growing large economy, India is witnessing capital outflows. What ails foreign investment?The energy-price shock from the war, rising interest rates, AI disruption fears in IT services and India's once-high market valuations have triggered a correction. Yet, underlying growth remains strong, with the PM citing nearly 8% economic growth and market earnings expected to rise at mid-teens rates in Q3.For long-term investors, the reset offers a better entry point, with lower valuations improving opportunities for new capital. Markets may turn fickle, but sustained earnings growth should draw global capital back. We see this as a temporary cold patch and will continue investing.Does currency depreciation worry you? What needs to be done?Currency depreciation has been the biggest headwind for foreign investors, making faster-growing businesses a better bet than bond-like assets with flat returns. We focus on high-growth healthcare, financial services, travel, digital infrastructure and real estate, including malls, offices and warehouses. India has made major strides in physical infrastructure, from airports and flyovers to GST reform, digital payments, legal systems and capital markets. These improvements have opened sectors once inaccessible to investors like us. So, rather than focus only on what govt can do better, it is important to stop and say they have done a heck of a job.Last year, you spoke about making delisting easier...India's 90% shareholding threshold for delisting is among the world's highest. Some of the rules are there to protect minority shareholders from promoters, but I think there's a way to do that and allow some of these companies to be privatised (delisted). Reforms can unlock consolidation, reward shareholders and improve companies' access to capital, as Japan's liberalisation has shown. It is like refreshing the farm by turning the soil.Yet, there have been some major capital-market strides. The REIT market, once non-existent, has attracted billions in capital, enabled us to bring five out of six REITs to the market and a $1.3 billion secondary sale in Knowledge Realty Trust in Aug. India is the world's second-most liquid IPO market after the US. Greater regulatory and tax certainty remains a work in progress, but govt deserves credit for opening markets to foreign capital. Further reforms could deepen access to capital.In AI, which areas would you look at investing in?AI opportunities span data centres, neoclouds and IT services. As traditional IT work shifts to AI, firms such as Mphasis, in which we own a large stake, are becoming AI-deployment partners, helping businesses redesign workflows rather than simply adopt tools such as Claude. Energy, especially renewables, will also be critical to powering both India's growth and its expanding data-centre infra.What risks do you see in AI investments?There is a risk of overinvestment and capital misallocation in AI, but financial commentary is too negative. Usage is surging, with tangible productivity gains. At IGI, our diamond and jewellery certification business in India, AI visualisation tools make grading 40% faster and enable each employee to process 30% more diamonds.Demand is exploding, driven by businesses and individuals using personalised AI agents, while computing capacity remains constrained by shortages of land, power, chips and capital. Unlike the '90s telecom boom, when speculative, leveraged infrastructure outstripped demand, today's data-centre build-out has strong demand, investment-grade hyperscalers as offtakers and little speculative construction. It is therefore financially sounder than booms seen in the past.But telecom companies did take a hit when Starlink announced its foray into telecom...AI's biggest risk is disruption to legacy businesses, already reflected in falling software and professional-services valuations and questions over the future of billable hours. Some AI investments will fail, but the technology's productivity gains and growth potential make significant infrastructure investment compelling.Investment in computing infrastructure can be compared to aviation, where aircraft retain value despite airline failures. Likewise, scarce AI computing capacity can be redeployed if an LLM company, software firm or hyperscaler fails. Markets may underestimate this residual value. Most data centres are backed by 15-20-year contracts with trillion-dollar-plus companies, limiting speculative, leveraged construction.You earlier spoke about risks arising from conflicts and macro factors. At the same time, many countries, including India, are seeing unrest. Do you see this impacting business?In a world connected by social media, we have seen a rise in social unrest, and I think that's going to be more of a staple of societies going forward because organising is now much easier. Part of it is also that we have seen a sharp rise in the cost of living, energy costs, food costs and housing costs, and I think this is something govts are going to need to respond to. I think in the West, we've made it very difficult to build new energy, new infrastructure and new housing, and I hope there's a push for some regulatory and permitting reform to accelerate investment in those areas. Technological upheaval also breeds anxiety, as during past industrial revolutions, while wars add to cost pressures. Hopefully, these wars will end at some point, and that should reduce pressure on prices. Economic growth is critical to getting countries through this, and countries will have to control the cost of living through fiscal discipline and low inflation.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Yikes': CoreWeave stock tanks on bond yield woes, CEO blames market acting 'irrationally'
articles.summary: CoreWeave stock fell more than 16% in morning trading on Wednesday, a day after a chart of its rising borrowing costs drew a one-word reply from Elon Musk: "...
articles.body:
CoreWeave ( CRWV ) stock fell 15% on Wednesday, a day after a chart of its rising borrowing costs gained traction on X.

Bloomberg, citing an internal memo, reports that the AI cloud company's CEO stated in a memo that the market is acting "irrationally."

"When you are building a new type of technology company, there will be periods of time when the market misunderstands and acts irrationally," CEO Mike Intrator wrote to staff. "We are confident in our business model, our customers, the extraordinary quality of our execution, and the relentless discipline around the financial engine we have built."

A bond's yield rises as its price falls, so a yield near 15% means investors want a steep return to lend CoreWeave money.

Intrator added that "factors like the weakness and delays surrounding the attempted IPOs and debt financings" of several CoreWeave rivals "are bleeding into the narrative around CoreWeave."

On Tuesday, venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya posted a chart showing that the yield on $1.25 billion of CoreWeave bonds due in 2032 "touched 15% today, then closed at a new high" of 14.5%.

"Is the AI buildout creating a private credit bubble?" Palihapitiya asked.

Musk, who owns the platform, replied with one word: " Yikes ."

The selling spread to other AI cloud stocks: Nebius ( NBIS ) fell 11%, Oracle ( ORCL ) dropped another 9%, and the following stocks sank more than 10%: DigitalOcean ( DOCN ), Hut 8 ( HUT ), Cipher ( CIFR ), TeraWulf ( WULF ), and IREN ( IREN ).

CoreWeave rents out Nvidia ( NVDA ) chips to AI companies and pays for much of that hardware with debt. The company's interest expense rose to $640 million in the second quarter from $267 million a year earlier, and it lost $626 million in the quarter, according to Yahoo Finance data. Revenue more than doubled over the same stretch to $2.58 billion.

Total debt reached about $52 billion at the end of June, up from about $15 billion a year earlier.

The company is clearly looking for cheaper money. CoreWeave is chasing insurers' vast pools of capital to fund its build-out, the Financial Times reported Wednesday.

Co-founder Brannin McBee, who leads CoreWeave's financing, told the FT that investment-grade ratings on more of its chip-backed debt would let it borrow from insurers, whose capital "is unlimited. Like, that's all the money in the world that sits in the insurance tranche."

McBee said CoreWeave will keep taking out chip-backed loans: "I don't look at that as scary debt at all. I look at that as accelerating debt and great debt."

articles.title: AI stocks drop after hot inflation report bolsters bets for Fed rate hikes
articles.summary: High-flying technology stocks are taking a bruising this week, as investors grow more skeptical about whether the AI boom will live up to expectations.
articles.body: High-flying technology stocks are taking a bruising this week, as investors grow more skeptical about whether the AI boom will live up to expectations. Stocks dropped on Wednesday, led by declines in the tech sector, after a hotter-than-expected inflation report bolstered bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates further. The S&P 500 fell 1.11% and the Nasdaq Composite fell 1.88%, each posting their worst day since July. Shares of companies involved in the AI data center buildout — the “picks and shovels” of the AI boom — stumbled, from semiconductor chipmakers to cloud providers. Marvell (MRVL), a chipmaker, fell 8.7%, Oracle (ORCL) sank 8.8% and Dell (DELL) dropped 11.3%. A benchmark index tracking semiconductor stocks fell 4.3%, putting it down roughly 12% over the past week. Nvidia (NVDA) fell 3.2%, leaving it down roughly 7.5% since hitting a record high earlier this month. Investors are digesting a range of concerns that are shaking sentiment around AI. Higher bond yields and sticky inflation have led to elevated borrowing costs, making the data center buildout more expensive. That’s raising concerns for the riskier, debt-heavy corners of the AI ecosystem. Meanwhile, chip stocks have had a rocky week after Chinese semiconductor company CXMT announced progress on advanced memory chips. That’s stoking concern about competition with US and South Korean manufacturers that have outlooks that are “priced to perfection,” according to analysts. Semiconductor stocks have soared on expectations that companies will lock in hefty profits because of the AI boom’s insatiable demand for chips. But a slowdown due to higher rates, or an increase in competition from China, could knock expectations for chipmakers’ future revenues and growth. The fate of the “picks and shovels” of the AI boom matters because tech and AI stocks have propelled the market to record highs this year. With other sectors of the market continuing to struggle under the pressure of higher bond yields, the stakes are higher for how these stocks perform. “There’s just so much good news priced into the chip sector right now that you’re going to find it’s susceptible to meandering without some fresh catalysts,” Steve Sosnick, chief strategist at Interactive Brokers, told CNN. After strong rallies earlier this year, Wall Street keeps raising the bar for expectations for chipmakers’ earnings, leaving room for disappointment or profit taking. “Trees don’t grow to the sky,” Sosnick said. “You can’t just go up forever and ever and ever, assuming that nothing is going to go wrong.” Investors are also watching riskier corners of AI. CoreWeave (CRWV), a so-called neocloud that is backed by Nvidia and leases compute power for the AI boom, plunged 15.5% on Wednesday after commentators raised concerns about a surge in the company’s bond yields. The company has tens of billions of dollars of debt on its balance sheet as it borrows money to try and expand its business and market share. As interest rates rise, it’s getting more expensive to finance that debt. The market is increasingly coming around to concerns about how companies taking on enormous debt are going to pay for it all, especially given concerns about delays to data center projects and uncertainty about the timeline of Anthropic’s and OpenAI’s initial public offerings, according to Sosnick. “There’s just so much money being thrown at this, and a lot of it has to be borrowed, and borrowed at increasingly high interest rates,” Sosnick said. “It’s an interesting conundrum.”

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The sale of govt stake in IDBI Bank will help increase its value, fully protect the interest of employees and directors nominated by the Centre and LIC will exit the board to give the new management a free hand, a top govt official told TOI on Wednesday.Hours after govt nod, Dipam secretary Arunish Chawla also vowed to move ahead with other transactions in the coming months and "not rest on past laurels". "We still haven't finished our work. We are further energised by the approval... We will continue to move ahead with the strategic transactions, and we will take Cabinet approvals to their logical conclusions. You will keep hearing from us from time to time," he said, without commenting on specific companies.Since 2016, the Union Cabinet has cleared three dozen strategic disinvestments but several of them, including BPCL and Shipping Corporation are no longer being pursued. Chawla dismissed suggestions that govt was not keen on privatisation of PSUs. "We are delivering on what has been approved by the Cabinet and we have completed five strategic sales in the last five years... Govt remains firmly on the track of reforms."The secretary said the new owners will bring fresh energy and private sector management practices and efficiency to boost IDBI Bank's performance, while expecting the transaction to be closed before end of the current financial year."We have spent the last one year discussing with the management, the employee associations, the qualified parties. We've brought everyone on board. Even today the service conditions of the IDBI Bank employees is decided by its board. The service conditions of all existing employees will be fully protected, all pensioners of IDBI Bank will be fully protected. There is a special pension fund set aside for this purpose and going forward, the new management will run the bank in consultation with the employees and its associations."Chawla said a lot of hard work has gone into ensuring that the transaction was cleared. After the setback in March, when the bids were rejected, the core group on disinvestment led by the Cabinet secretary and DIPAM went back to the drawing board. "We relied completely on professional advice. When the stock market price is extremely volatile and the stock is very narrowly traded, it tends to misalign the intrinsic value," he said.So, govt studied global examples and went for relative valuation by what is called market multiple method or moon charts methodology. The market multiples of comparable entities are used to compute the fair market value. Separately, an asset valuation method was used based on the assets and liabilities."Because the book value of IDBI Bank was low, the professional agencies converted the asset and liabilities on the books, including financial assets and physical assets like land and buildings, into their fair replacement value. In addition, they valued intangibles like the economic value of the banking licence, customer relationship, which is built on its branch network, the brand value and added all this up to the book value to arrive at the net asset value or the fair value asset value," Chawla added.Using the average of the two valuations worked out to Rs 75.99 a share, while the winning best bid was Rs 81 a share, resulting in CCEA clearing the Farifax offer."After six months of hard work and through a collective decision and multi-lauyered decision making process, where everyone's views were taken on board and professional agencies were allowed to do their job, we have been able to find a way forward... articles.title: As inflation rises, more than 40 percent say they struggle to pay for basic necessities: Pew
articles.summary: More than 4 in 10 Americans said they are struggling to afford basic living costs amid rising inflation levels in the country, according to polling data released Wednesday. The Pew Research Center surveys, which were conducted in late July and August, found that 44 percent of U.S. adults reported struggling to pay for basic necessities…
articles.body:
More than 4 in 10 Americans said they are struggling to afford basic living costs amid rising inflation levels in the country, according to polling data released Wednesday.

The Pew Research Center surveys , which were conducted in late July and August, found that 44 percent of U.S. adults reported struggling to pay for basic necessities like medical care, rent or mortgage, transportation and food.

Rising costs had an even greater impact on lower income Americans, as 71 percent of those surveyed said they struggled with costs for at least one of these expense categories.

Additionally, 60 percent of people said they did not have enough income to “lead the kind of life they want,” while 53 percent said they did not have sufficient emergency funds.

The inflation rate in August was 3.4 percent , down from 3.7 percent in July. Since then, the Bureau of Labor Statistics has reported further increases to the consumer price index, including a 0.6 percent increase in September.

Gas prices have accounted for a sizable share of the inflation rate increases, as the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war placed a sustained strain on global energy supplies.

A gallon of regular gas was around $4.33 a gallon in the U.S. on Wednesday afternoon, up from about $3.08 a year ago, according to AAA . The average cost of diesel has also spiked to more than $6 a gallon — an increase of more than $2 from last year.

President Trump has attempted to calm concerns about rising costs of living amid this conflict and his administration’s tariff fight with Canada ahead of the midterm elections, in which affordability is expected to be a top issue for voters at the ballot box.

During a Tuesday campaign rally in Alaska, the president did not offer hope that the months-long conflict was nearing a close, telling the crowd he has “had it” with Iran’s leaders and added that his administration was “going to do a number” on the country.

The Pew report released Wednesday was based on findings from two surveys among a sample of 5,166 U.S. adults with a margin of error of approximately 1.6 percentage points. One poll was conducted from Aug. 24-30, while the other was conducted from July 20 to Aug. 9.

Long-dated bond yields, tied to borrowing costs, rose before trimming gains after September's inflation data was released.

That put pressure on Tech ( XLK ) stocks, which were already on jittery ground amid elevated yields, rising debt, possible disruptions to AI buildouts, and overall concerns about a bubble.

On Wednesday, worries about borrowing costs also hit the AI trade.

The stock's sharp sell-off highlighted concerns about the company's debt-heavy balance sheet and whether it can scale fast enough to manage its growing interest expense.

Any slowdown in AI spending could spell trouble for chip makers, which have been the main beneficiaries of infrastructure spending as hyperscalers race to build out data centers.

articles.title: Eight US states sue OpenAI, claiming ChatGPT harms young users
articles.summary: Oct 14 (Reuters) - A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts ‌across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has ca...
articles.body:
Oct 14 (Reuters) - A bipartisan group of eight states said on Wednesday they had sued OpenAI in courts ‌across the country over harms they say ChatGPT has caused ‌to their residents, alleging the chatbot has coached its users — including teenagers — to harm themselves or others.

Attorneys ​general from the states, which include Iowa, Kansas and Arizona, filed the lawsuits independently in state courts, claiming ChatGPT is designed to be agreeable and engaging to earn the trust of users. But the chatbot reinforces delusions, encourages ‌dangerous behavior and assists ⁠users in planning violence like mass shootings, the lawsuits claim.

The lawsuits represent the most significant coordinated state action against ⁠an artificial intelligence company, adding to a wave of legal challenges OpenAI faces as it prepares for a public listing. Florida's attorney general filed the first ​such state ​suit in June.

The lawsuits accuse the ​company of violating state consumer ‌protection laws by misleading users about the safety of ChatGPT. The states also allege that the company created a public nuisance by endangering the health of their residents.

The lawsuits seek orders forcing OpenAI to make changes to how ChatGPT works. Among other things, the states want the company ‌barred from developing AI models that can ​improve themselves unless it can ensure those models ​are aligned with human ​values.

The states, which also include Arkansas, Idaho, Montana, Nebraska and ‌West Virginia, are also seeking civil monetary ​penalties for OpenAI's ​violations of state law as well as damages.

A spokesperson for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The company is ​also facing dozens of ‌lawsuits by private plaintiffs, alleging ChatGPT helped users plan mass shootings ​or other violence.

(Reporting by Diana Novak Jones; Editing by Chris ​Reese, Alexia Garamfalvi and Aurora Ellis)

articles.title: Hot inflation data puts Fed in complicated spot
articles.summary: Inflation data for September indicates price pressures are still weighing on the economy, putting Federal Reserve officials in a tricky position ahead of their decision on interest rates later this month. Annual inflation was 3.7 percent last month, as measured by the consumer price index (CPI), an increase from 3.4 percent in August and the…
articles.body:
Inflation data for September indicates price pressures are still weighing on the economy, putting Federal Reserve officials in a tricky position ahead of their decision on interest rates later this month.

Annual inflation was 3.7 percent last month, as measured by the consumer price index (CPI), an increase from 3.4 percent in August and the highest mark since May.

Investors responded to the data by increasing the odds of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) officials raising rates by a quarter point at their next meeting, set for Oct. 27-28.

Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, wrote Wednesday on the social platform X that the CPI data “puts an October hike back on the table.”

The data provides the central bank with further evidence that inflation is not approaching its 2 percent target, as Fed Chair Kevin Warsh is set to speak at a gathering of finance ministers in Thailand on Friday local time.

Heather Long, the chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said Wednesday the inflation data makes the Fed’s decision on interest rates a “coin flip” between hiking rates by a quarter point for a second straight meeting and holding them between 3.75 percent and 4 percent.

“It’s tricky. It will be a hot conversation in that room,” Long told The Hill.

Traders on Tuesday were pricing in a nearly 78 percent chance of the FOMC holding rates, according to the CME FedWatch tool . But after the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) released September’s inflation report, those odds sank to roughly a 67 percent chance as of Wednesday afternoon.

The latest inflation data shows that energy prices rose 5.2 percent from August to September and were up 20.4 percent year over year. Gas prices were up 9.1 percent from August, accounting for more than 50 percent of the overall rise in prices.

Core prices, which don’t include more volatile food and energy costs, were up 2.6 percent last month from September 2025. Food prices held steady from August to September, the BLS reported.

Brooks noted Wednesday that wireless services, which rose by 5.9 percent from July to August, contributed heavily to the latter month’s core inflation reading of 2.4 percent. That gave the Fed a “reasonable excuse to pause” and hold rates steady later this month, he argued.

But the latest CPI data showed monthly price spikes for an array of products, including 0.7 percent for used cars and trucks, 0.3 percent for apparel and 0.3 percent for medical care services.

Taken together, the numbers indicate inflation is a “lot more broad-based and entrenched” than economists thought, Long argued.

“It’s a real squeeze. … Many Americans are financially worse off, certainly, than they were six months ago. But many Americans are worse off than they were a year ago,” she said.

After the FOMC unanimously voted to raise rates in mid-September, committee officials have signaled future rate hikes are coming — while noting they need to evaluate data as it trickles in.

Beth Hammack, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland, said Monday that “demand-side” inflationary pressures, such as from the artificial intelligence buildout, are “not self-correcting” and will persist even if energy prices fall upon an end to the Iran war.

“Because of the breadth of inflationary pressures, my baseline forecast is that it will take some time for inflation to return to 2 percent, even with appropriate monetary policy,” Hammack said at a National Association for Business Economics meeting.

Warsh avoided forecasting future monetary policy decisions after the Fed raised rates last month, telling reporters he was “ill-prepared” to do so.

The Fed chair will deliver his first remarks since his post-hike press conference on Friday, when he will speak alongside International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva in Thailand.

Joe Mazzola, the head trading and derivatives strategist at Charles Schwab, wrote Wednesday it is “unclear” whether Warsh will discuss policy issues in Thailand.

Looming over the heads of FOMC officials are President Trump’s repeated calls for them to lower interest rates. While he has praised Warsh, the president said last week other Fed officials “would like to see the country do badly.”

Plus, the next FOMC meeting is set for less than a week before the midterms, with Republicans fighting economic headwinds as they try to hold on to Congress for the final two years of Trump’s term.

There is precedent for the Fed hiking rates right before the midterms — officials did so in 2022 , after inflation reached a 40-year high earlier that year.

But Long, citing the political implications of another hike, predicted that the FOMC will keep rates steady later this month before hiking in early December.

“When it’s that close of a call, this is the one meeting where the election matters,” she said. “I know they like to say they’re apolitical, and generally they are, but … the bar is extra high to hike a week before an election.”

Long added, “If there were a real need to do it, they would do it. But when you’re sitting here and it’s kind of 50-50, it’s hard [not] to look around the table and say, ‘Gee, if we wait till December.’ … It’s not like the economy is going to fall apart if they wait till December.”

articles.title: Inflation rose slightly in September
articles.summary: Welcome to The Hill’s Business & Economy newsletter {beacon} Business & Economy Business & Economy The Big Story Inflation in September rose to 3.7 percent: BLS Inflation rose slightly in September after holding steady the month prior, new data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) showed Wednesday. © Nam Y. articles.body:
Inflation in September rose to 3.7 percent: BLS

Inflation rose slightly in September after holding steady the month prior, new data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) showed Wednesday.

The consumer price index (CPI) increased 0.6 percent last month and was up 3.7 percent relative to September 2025. That marked an increase from August, when annual inflation sat at 3.4 percent.

The popular inflation metric was expected to rise by 0.5 percent in September and increase slightly to 3.6 percent year over year, the Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland’s “Nowcast” projected on Tuesday.

Gas prices, which rose 9.1 percent in September, accounted for more than half of the monthly increase in inflation, according to the BLS.

Energy prices overall ticked up by 5.2 percent last month after rising by 2.1 percent in August. Food prices, meanwhile, held steady in September and were up 2.5 percent from 12 months prior.

Fuel costs have remained elevated amid the Iran war, with President Trump’s efforts to lower diesel and gas prices not bearing fruit so far.

A gallon of regular gas costs roughly $4.33 as of Wednesday morning, up from $2.98 two days before the U.S. and Israel launched the war, according to data from AAA. Diesel also costs about $6.30 per gallon, an increase of roughly $2.64 relative to a year ago, AAA reported.

Trump has not indicated he will end the war soon, saying Wednesday he has “had it” with Iran’s leaders.

“We’re going to do a number [on Iran],” the president said during a campaign rally in Alaska.

Core annual inflation, which does not include more volatile food or energy prices, was 2.6 percent — higher than the Cleveland Fed’s projection of 2.4 percent, which is where it stood in August.

Heather Long , chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, noted the spike in inflation “was largely driven by rising gas and diesel prices” along with higher airfares and prices for used cars.

“The big problem = Inflation rose 3.7% in the past year, wiping out 3% average wage gains ,” she wrote Wednesday on the social platform X.
