articles.title: Rs 53k crore IDBI stake sale with LIC takes government past selloff target
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Govt and LIC will sell a combined 60.7% in IDBI Bank for Rs 52,878 crore to an arm of Fairfax Financial Holdings, which is controlled by
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Govt and LIC will sell a combined 60.7% in IDBI Bank for Rs 52,878 crore to an arm of Fairfax Financial Holdings, which is controlled by Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa, that will result in the largest-ever financial sector FDI in the country. The transaction will help govt scale the disinvestment and asset monetisation target of Rs 80,000 crore for the current fiscal year.The Centre will sell 30.48% to 10955230 Canada Inc, while LIC will offload 30.24% after the cabinet committee on economic affairs cleared the transaction on Wednesday, five years after the process started and seven months after the earlier bids by Fairfax and Emirates NBD were rejected. Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the "strategic restructuring" - as opposed to strategic sale - will result in govt retaining a 15% stake. LIC will have 19% of the equity capital, which will have to be diluted to 15% in two years as the life insurer is also the promoter of a housing finance company.Fairfax gets 2 yrs to decide on CSB stakeAfter signing the share purchase agreement, the Canadian company will have to make an open offer for the 5.3% stake held by the public. Fairfax, which will present its credentials to RBI in the coming weeks, will have to decide on its 40% holding in Catholic Syrian Bank — whether it will sell the shares or merge the bank with IDBI Bank.Over the next 15 years, the Canadian company will be required to pare its stake to 26%. The sale comes with a lock-in period of five years with the Canadian company allowed to retain the brand for three years.Although the decision was announced after the stock market closed, IDBI shares closed 9% higher at Rs 90.44 on BSE. “Having supported the bank’s recovery, we are now enabling its next phase of growth through the infusion of FDI while retaining a minority stake. This will not only strengthen the banking ecosystem but also help banking services surpass global benchmarks. It reinforces that India’s growth story is strong, its economy is resilient, and the government’s commitment to reform is unwavering,” Sitharaman said in a post on X. While strategic sale is part of NDA govt’s policy, before IDBI, there have only been three transactions that went through — Air India (2021-22), Ferro Scrap Nigam (2024) and Indian Medicines Pharmaceuticals Corporation (May 2026).Govt will completely exit the board of the bank after the sale, which was first discussed in 2016, but was put off, before restarting in 2020 with the preliminary information memorandum issued in Oct 2022. From five players, the field narrowed to two, which submitted their bids that were rejected in March as they were below the reserve price of 94.42 a share, influenced by the market price which swung between Rs 42.40 when expression of interest was sought and Rs 108. 12 on Jan 8, before bids were invited. Given the volatility in the narrowly traded scrip, with only 5.3% public holding, govt opted to use relative valuation by the market multiple method. articles.title: OpenAI accuses former employee of leaking intel on AI device to Apple
articles.summary: OpenAI is accusing a former employee of stealing intellectual property related to an unreleased device and later sharing some of the information with Apple.
articles.body: OpenAI is accusing a former employee of stealing intellectual property related to an unreleased device and later sharing some of the information with Apple. The employee, OpenAI alleges, had previously worked at Apple, then joined OpenAI for six months, before going back to Apple, according to a court filing from OpenAI on Wednesday. The company said the employee downloaded over 100 highly confidential files to his personal accounts before rejoining Apple. The transferred files include “detailed images of the unreleased device(s), as well as highly confidential engineering and manufacturing data about the device(s),” according to the filing. The last file was sent in June on the employee’s final day, OpenAI alleges. OpenAI went on to claim the former employee, who it did not name, “made a presentation about OpenAI’s product plans to Apple’s senior leadership, including Apple’s vice president of operations in Asia.” “That presentation appears to have happened months ago—and now, armed with that information, Apple is making a new push into AI-enabled products,” OpenAI wrote in the filing. Apple told CNN it has found no evidence to support the allegations and that it has strict policies in place to make sure new employees don’t use confidential information from previous workplaces. The company also said it would work with OpenAI to remediate any of OpenAI’s information found on Apple’s systems. Apple accused OpenAI of trying to create a distraction from the original claims of their case. The allegations came as part of a filing in an ongoing lawsuit that Apple brought against OpenAI in July, alleging the AI company stole the iPhone maker’s trade secrets to develop its own gadgets. Apple alleged in its original filing that former employees who went to work for OpenAI downloaded confidential files, and urged job candidates to bring Apple parts to interviews at OpenAI. OpenAI has denied the claims, saying Apple hasn’t been able to identify any stolen trade secrets and has sought to dismiss the case. Both companies are racing to create AI-enabled devices. This week, Apple announced HomeView, its biggest push into the smart home market in nearly a decade with a revamped version of Siri, making it a critical piece of Apple’s AI strategy. OpenAI is working on an AI-enabled device, reported to be a small screen-free smart speaker. Last year, OpenAI brought on former Apple product design chief Jonny Ive and his company, io, to take over design and creative responsibilities across the company. While engineers and researchers regularly switch companies in Silicon Valley, Apple said in a court filing that OpenAI has hired more than 400 of its former employees. CNN’s Lisa Eadicicco contributed to this report.
